section: Energy policy of India - Integrated Energy Policy, NITI Aayog National Energy Policy, energy transition targets
subsections: Energy policy documents - year and drafting body
Energy transition targets - 2030 and net zero

accepted.s: The Integrated Energy Policy was prepared by which body and in which year was it issued?
o: Planning Commission expert committee under Kirit Parikh, 2006
accepted.x: The Integrated Energy Policy was prepared in 2006 by an expert committee of the Planning Commission under Kirit Parikh. It was approved in 2008.
accepted.tq: Match the document with its drafting body and distinguish the preparation year from the approval year.
accepted.sec: Energy policy documents - year and drafting body

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: India Energy Security Scenarios 2047 — NITI Aayog — 2014–15
Draft National Energy Policy — Ministry of Power — 2017
Integrated Energy Policy — Ministry of Power — 2008
accepted.x: India Energy Security Scenarios 2047 was prepared by NITI Aayog in 2014–15. The Draft National Energy Policy was prepared by NITI Aayog in 2017, while the National Electricity Policy 2005 was issued by the Ministry of Power.
accepted.tq: Use document–year–body association and reject swapped institutional authorities.
accepted.sec: Energy policy documents - year and drafting body

accepted.s:
The Draft National Energy Policy prepared by NITI Aayog has which of the following as its objectives?
1. Access to energy at affordable prices
2. Improved energy security and independence
3. Greater sustainability
4. Economic growth

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The four objectives are affordable access, improved security and independence, greater sustainability and economic growth.
accepted.tq: Recognise a complete objectives list; the comprehensive option contains all four stated objectives.
accepted.sec: Energy policy documents - year and drafting body

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Draft National Electricity Policy 2026:
1. It is issued by the Ministry of Power.
2. It replaces the National Electricity Policy, 2005.
3. It includes hybrid renewable energy, battery energy storage systems, smart grids and Time-of-Day tariffs.
4. It sets a pumped-storage target of 100 GW by 2047.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 is a Ministry of Power document replacing the 2005 policy and includes the listed technologies, tariff reform and the 100 GW pumped-storage target by 2047.
accepted.tq: Test a policy document through its issuing ministry, replacement relationship and distinctive provisions.
accepted.sec: Energy policy documents - year and drafting body

accepted.s: The target of 100 GW of pumped-storage capacity by 2047 is associated with which policy document?
accepted.x: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 sets a target of 100 GW of pumped-storage capacity by 2047.
accepted.tq: Link the distinctive numerical target to the correct policy document.
accepted.sec: Energy policy documents - year and drafting body

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the major areas of intervention identified in the energy policy framework?
o: Exclusive expansion of urban metro rail networks
Oil and gas supply, including domestic exploration and production and overseas acreage
accepted.x: The listed interventions include energy consumption, demand-side efficiency and decarbonisation, coal, electricity, oil and gas supply, and oil refining and distribution. Exclusive expansion of urban metro rail networks is not listed as an intervention.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the stated intervention list rather than selecting a merely related energy activity.
accepted.sec: Energy policy documents - year and drafting body

accepted.s: Fossil fuels account for approximately what share of India’s commercial primary energy supply, and what associated trend is highlighted?
o: Nearly 90%, with increasing dependence on imports
accepted.x: Fossil fuels constitute nearly 90% of commercial primary energy supply and are increasingly imported. Reducing fossil-fuel use therefore supports both sustainability and energy security.
accepted.tq: Combine the approximate share with the direction of import dependence; reject extreme percentage claims.
accepted.sec: Energy policy documents - year and drafting body

accepted.s: According to the NITI Aayog projection based on the India Energy Security Scenarios, energy demand between 2012 and 2040 was expected to increase by:
o: 3.5–4.0 times, while electricity demand increases three-fold
accepted.x: The projection indicated that total energy demand would rise 2.7–3.2 times from 2012 to 2040, while electricity demand would increase 4.5-fold.
accepted.tq: Preserve the paired projection values and avoid reversing the total-energy and electricity figures.
accepted.sec: Energy policy documents - year and drafting body

accepted.s: Primary energy import dependence was projected to change from 31% in 2012 to which range by 2040?
accepted.x: The projection placed primary energy import dependence at 31% in 2012 and 36–55% by 2040.
accepted.tq: Test the starting value and projected range together, with nearby percentage distractors.
accepted.sec: Energy policy documents - year and drafting body

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the projected change in India’s per capita energy use?
o: From 684 kgoe in 2014 to 1055–1184 kgoe in 2022
From 1055 kgoe in 2014 to 521–684 kgoe in 2040
From 521 kgoe in 2014 to 1055–1184 kgoe in 2040
From 521 kgoe in 2012 to 2040 kgoe in 2040
accepted.x: Per capita energy use was projected to rise from 521 kgoe in 2014 to 1055–1184 kgoe by 2040.
accepted.tq: Check both endpoints and the projection year; the distractors swap years or alter the units and figures.
accepted.sec: Energy policy documents - year and drafting body

accepted.s: The projected target for the manufacturing sector’s share in GDP was to increase from 16% to:
accepted.x: The projection of that period aimed to raise manufacturing’s share of GDP from 16% to 25% by 2022.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the target percentage from the target year in a time-bound projection.
accepted.sec: Energy policy documents - year and drafting body

accepted.s: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas target concerning oil imports was to reduce them by what amount from the 2014–15 level by 2022?
accepted.x: The target was to reduce oil imports by 10% from the 2014–15 level by 2022.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact percentage and base year rather than confusing it with a broader import-dependence projection.
accepted.sec: Energy policy documents - year and drafting body

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs concerning electricity-sector policy is correctly matched?
o: Electricity Act — 2003; National Electricity Policy — 2005; Tariff Policy — 2006, revised in 2016
Electricity Act — 2005; National Electricity Policy — 2003; Tariff Policy — 2017
Electricity Act — 2006; National Electricity Policy — 2008; Tariff Policy — 2014, revised in 2022
Electricity Act — 2017; National Electricity Policy — 2016; Tariff Policy — 2005, revised in 2006
accepted.x: The relevant sequence is the Electricity Act 2003, National Electricity Policy 2005 and Tariff Policy 2006, with the Tariff Policy revised in 2016.
accepted.tq: Arrange and associate closely related legislation and policies by year, including the later revision.
accepted.sec: Energy policy documents - year and drafting body

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between the new and earlier electricity policies?
o: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 replaces the National Electricity Policy 2005.
The Draft National Electricity Policy 2017 replaced the Tariff Policy 2006.
The National Electricity Policy 2005 replaced the Draft National Electricity Policy 2026.
The Tariff Policy 2016 replaced the Electricity Act 2003.
accepted.x: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026, issued by the Ministry of Power, is intended to replace the National Electricity Policy 2005.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a policy, a tariff policy and an Act by testing the direction of replacement.
accepted.sec: Energy policy documents - year and drafting body

accepted.s: The energy-intensity targets for 208 industrial units under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 are intended to feed into which mechanism?
o: The National Green Hydrogen Mission alone
The State Energy and Climate Index
accepted.x: Greenhouse-gas emission-intensity targets for 208 industrial units under the Energy Conservation Act 2001 feed into the domestic carbon market.
accepted.tq: Link the statutory target, the number of industrial units and the specific market mechanism.
accepted.sec: Energy policy documents - year and drafting body

accepted.s:
The Panchamrit commitments announced at COP26 in Glasgow include which of the following?
1. 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030
2. Meeting 50% of energy needs from renewable energy by 2030
3. Achieving net zero emissions by 2070

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Panchamrit commitments include 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030, 50% of energy needs from renewable energy by 2030 and net zero emissions by 2070. They were announced at COP26 in Glasgow in 2021.
accepted.tq: Use the complete set of three headline commitments and distinguish energy share from installed-capacity targets.
accepted.sec: Energy transition targets - 2030 and net zero

accepted.s: India’s target of 50% non-fossil installed power capacity by 2030 was achieved in:
accepted.x: India achieved 50% non-fossil installed capacity in June 2025, five years ahead of the 2030 target.
accepted.tq: Test the early-achievement date against the original target year.
accepted.sec: Energy transition targets - 2030 and net zero

accepted.s: As of 30 November 2025, which of the following correctly describes India’s installed power capacity and non-fossil capacity?
o: 509.64 GW total and 246.90 GW non-fossil, constituting 48.45%
470 GW total and 262.74 GW non-fossil, constituting 47%
542 GW total and 283.46 GW non-fossil, constituting 52.27%
509.64 GW total and 262.74 GW non-fossil, constituting 51.55%
accepted.x: As of 30 November 2025, total installed capacity was 509.64 GW and non-fossil capacity was 262.74 GW, or 51.55%. The 542 GW and 283.46 GW figures relate to 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate closely spaced status dates and reject figures belonging to a different year.
accepted.sec: Energy transition targets - 2030 and net zero

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the 30 November 2025 installed-capacity data?
o: Renewable energy including large hydro — 153.96 GW
accepted.x: The 30 November 2025 capacity composition included 246.90 GW thermal, 8.78 GW nuclear and 253.96 GW renewable energy including large hydro, making 262.74 GW non-fossil capacity.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure capacity pair and identify the options that alter a component figure.
accepted.sec: Energy transition targets - 2030 and net zero

accepted.s: By 2026, India’s installed capacity and non-fossil capacity were reported as approximately:
accepted.x: By 2026, installed capacity was reported at 542 GW and non-fossil capacity at 283.46 GW, constituting 52.27%. Renewable energy had crossed 200 GW.
accepted.tq: Keep total capacity, non-fossil capacity and percentage in their proper order.
accepted.sec: Energy transition targets - 2030 and net zero

accepted.s: By 2026, India was ranked third in solar energy and fourth in wind energy. Which option correctly states this ranking?
o: First in solar and second in wind
Second in solar and third in wind
Fourth in solar and third in wind
Third in solar and fourth in wind
accepted.x: India was reported to rank third globally in solar energy and fourth in wind energy by 2026.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing the paired rankings in a comparison-based question.
accepted.sec: Energy transition targets - 2030 and net zero

accepted.s: The new NDC for 2031–35 proposes which combination of targets?
o: 70% non-fossil capacity and a 35% reduction in emissions intensity by 2030
50% non-fossil capacity and a 45% reduction in emissions intensity by 2030
47% non-fossil capacity and a 60% reduction in emissions intensity by 2035
60% non-fossil capacity and a 47% reduction in emissions intensity by 2035
accepted.x: The new NDC for 2031–35 proposes 60% non-fossil capacity and a 47% cut in emissions intensity by 2035.
accepted.tq: Match both the target percentages and the common target year instead of mixing them with the updated 2022 NDC.
accepted.sec: Energy transition targets - 2030 and net zero

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s updated NDC of 2022:
1. It committed to reducing emissions intensity by 45% by 2030 from the 2005 level.
2. It set a target of 50% installed power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030.
3. The earlier emissions-intensity target was 33–35%.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 2022 updated NDC raised the emissions-intensity reduction target to 45% over the 2005 level and retained the 50% non-fossil installed-capacity target for 2030. The earlier target was 33–35%.
accepted.tq: Contrast the updated target with the earlier range while retaining the common 2030 horizon.
accepted.sec: Energy transition targets - 2030 and net zero

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the National Green Hydrogen Mission?
o: An outlay of ₹19,744 crore and a production target of 50 MMT per year
An outlay of ₹19,744 crore and a production target of 5 MMT per year
An outlay of ₹1,974 crore and a production target of 5 MMT by 2030 only
An outlay of ₹9,744 crore and a production target of 10 MMT per year
accepted.x: The National Green Hydrogen Mission has an outlay of ₹19,744 crore and targets production of 5 million metric tonnes per year.
accepted.tq: Pair the financial outlay with the annual production target and reject altered units or magnitudes.
accepted.sec: Energy transition targets - 2030 and net zero

accepted.s: India’s stated goal of achieving energy independence is associated with which year?
accepted.x: India has set the goal of achieving energy independence by 2047. Net zero emissions is the separate 2070 target.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the energy-independence year from the net-zero year.
accepted.sec: Energy transition targets - 2030 and net zero

accepted.s: The Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy of India was submitted to which body at which event?
accepted.x: India submitted its Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy to the UNFCCC at COP27 in 2022.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the international body, conference number and year.
accepted.sec: Energy transition targets - 2030 and net zero

accepted.s:
The Andhra Pradesh Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024 aims at which of the following?
1. More than 160 GW of clean energy
2. Investment of ₹10 lakh crore
3. Creation of 7.5 lakh jobs
4. A net-zero State by 2047

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024 targets more than 160 GW of clean energy, ₹10 lakh crore investment, 7.5 lakh jobs and a net-zero State by 2047.
accepted.tq: Test a state policy through its complete package of capacity, investment, employment and net-zero targets.
accepted.sec: State Energy and Climate Index - AP rank

accepted.s: Under the Renewable Purchase Obligation mechanism, which entities are required to purchase a prescribed share of electricity from renewable energy sources?
o: DISCOMs and open-access or captive users
Only generating companies owned by the Union Government
Only households consuming less than 100 kW
accepted.x: RPO requires DISCOMs and open-access or captive users to purchase a prescribed share of power from renewable energy sources. State Electricity Regulatory Commissions fix the obligation.
accepted.tq: Identify the obligated entities separately from the authority that sets the obligation.
accepted.sec: RPO, green energy open access, ISTS waiver

accepted.s: Which body is empowered under the Electricity Act, 2003 to fix Renewable Purchase Obligations?
o: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy alone
accepted.x: The Electricity Act 2003 enables State Electricity Regulatory Commissions to fix Renewable Purchase Obligations.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish the regulator from ministries and technical bodies.
accepted.sec: RPO, green energy open access, ISTS waiver

accepted.s: The Green Energy Open Access Rules, 2022 reduced the threshold for obtaining open access to green power to:
accepted.x: The Green Energy Open Access Rules 2022, issued by the Ministry of Power, reduced the threshold for green-power open access to 100 kW.
accepted.tq: Recall the specific threshold and distinguish it from larger conventional open-access limits.
accepted.sec: RPO, green energy open access, ISTS waiver

accepted.s: Which ministry issued the Green Energy Open Access Rules, 2022?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
accepted.x: The Green Energy Open Access Rules, 2022 were issued by the Ministry of Power.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-authority trap by distinguishing the issuing ministry from related ministries.
accepted.sec: RPO, green energy open access, ISTS waiver

accepted.s: Fiscal incentives for States linked to renewable-energy adoption are intended primarily to:
o: Discourage power-purchase agreements for renewable energy
Promote greater renewable-energy adoption and more power-purchase agreements
Replace all State electricity regulators with a central body
accepted.x: Linking fiscal incentives to renewable-energy adoption is intended to promote adoption and encourage more power-purchase agreements. The policy was accepted by the Finance and Power ministries.
accepted.tq: Infer the policy purpose from the incentive design and reject options that reverse its effect.
accepted.sec: RPO, green energy open access, ISTS waiver
